sources.title: VOA Special English - 'Lightning Never Strikes the Same Place...
sources.excerpt: When speaking about lightning, we have another common expression: Lightning never strikes the same place

reasoning: The claim is a well-known scientific myth. In reality, lightning frequently strikes the same location multiple times, particularly if it is a tall, pointed, or isolated object. According to the National Weather Service (NWS), the Empire State Building in New York City is struck by lightning an average of 23 to 25 times every year. From a physics perspective, tall conductors polarize under a storm cloud, generating "upward leaders" of positive charge that easily connect with the descending "stepped leaders" of negative charge from the cloud, making them highly receptive to repeated strikes.
